arxiv-1705-02831.title: What is a noncommutative topos? Thanks: Karin Cvetko-Vah acknowledges the financial support from the Slovenian Research Agency (research core funding No. P1-0222) Thanks: Jens Hemelaer is a Ph.D. fellow of the Research Foundation - Flanders (FWO)
arxiv-1705-02831.creator: Karin Cvetko-Vah, Jens Hemelaer, Lieven Le Bruyn
arxiv-1705-02831.description: Abstract . In [ 1 ] noncommutative frames were introduced, generalizing the usual notion of frames of open sets of a topological space. In this paper we extend this notion to noncommutative versions of Grothendieck topologies and their associated noncommutative toposes of sheaves of sets. For Fred Van Oystaeyen on his 70th birthday. 1.

arxiv-1812-07642.title: Impact of the purposeful kinesis on running waves
arxiv-1812-07642.creator: N. Çabukoǧlu
arxiv-1812-07642.description: Abstract The basic model of purposeful kinesis was developed recently (Gorban & Çabukoǧlu, Ecol. Complex. 2018, 33, 75–83) on the basis of the “Let well enough alone" idea. According to this model the diffusion drops while the reproduction coefficient is increasing.

arxiv-2012-12173.title: Constructive and Destructive Interference of Kerker-type Scattering in an Ultra-thin Silicon Huygens Metasurface
arxiv-2012-12173.creator: Xia Zhang, Jing Li, John F. Donegan, A. Louise Bradley
arxiv-2012-12173.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Xia Zhang, Jing Li, John F. Donegan, A. Louise Bradley. High refractive index dielectric nanoparticles have provided a new platform for exotic light manipulation through the interference of multipole modes. The Kerker effect is one example of a Huygens source design. Rather than exploiting interference between the electric dipole and magnetic dipole, as in many conventional Huygens source designs, we explore Kerker-type suppressed backward scattering mediated by the dominant electric dipole, toroidal dipole and magnetic quadrupole.

arxiv-2012-14647.title: Generalized Thomas–Yau Uniqueness Theorems
arxiv-2012-14647.creator: Yohsuke Imagi
arxiv-2012-14647.description: Abstract We generalize Thomas–Yau’s uniqueness theorem [ 17 , Theorem 4.3] in two ways. We prove a stronger statement for special Lagranigans and include minimal Lagrangians in Kähler–Einstein manifolds or more generally J J -minimal Lagrangians introduced by Lotay and Pacini [ 13 , 14 ] .

arxiv-2107-00098.title: Metallic Hydrogen: A Liquid Superconductor?
arxiv-2107-00098.creator: Craig M. Tenney, Zachary F. Croft, Jeffrey M. McMahon
arxiv-2107-00098.description: Abstract Metallic hydrogen is expected to exhibit remarkable physics. Of particular interest in this work is the possibility of high-temperature superconductivity. Comparing calculations of the superconducting critical temperatures of the solid phase to melting temperatures over a range of pressures leads to an interesting question: Will the solid, in a superconducting state, melt to a liquid that remains a superconductor?

arxiv-2206-03545.title: Code-DKT: A Code-based Knowledge Tracing Model for Programming Tasks
arxiv-2206-03545.creator: Yang Shi, Min Chi, Tiffany Barnes, Thomas W. Price
arxiv-2206-03545.description: Abstract Knowledge tracing (KT) models are a popular approach for predicting students’ future performance at practice problems using their prior attempts. Though many innovations have been made in KT, most models including the state-of-the-art Deep KT (DKT) mainly leverage each student’s response either as correct or incorrect, ignoring its content .

arxiv-2402-16952.title: Orbital selective order and ℤ 3 \mathbb{Z}_{3} Potts nematicity from a non-Fermi liquid
arxiv-2402-16952.creator: YuZheng Xie, Andrew Hardy, Arun Paramekanti
arxiv-2402-16952.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by YuZheng Xie, Andrew Hardy, Arun Paramekanti. Motivated by systems where a high temperature non-Fermi liquid gives way to low temperature ℤ 3 \mathbb{Z}_{3} Potts nematic order, we studied a three-orbital Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model in the large- N N limit. In the single-site limit, this model exhibits a spontaneous orbital-selective transition which preserves average particle-hole symmetry, with two orbitals becoming insulators while the third orbital remains a non-Fermi liquid down to zero temperature.

arxiv-2409-19675.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Simulation-based Inference in Computational Biology
arxiv-2409-19675.creator: Xiaoyu Wang, Ryan P. Kelly, Adrianne L. Jenner, David J. Warne, Christopher Drovandi 1 School of Mathematical Sciences, Queensland University of Technology, Brisbane, QLD, Australia 2 Centre for Data Science, Queensland University of Technology, Brisbane, QLD, Australia
arxiv-2409-19675.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xiaoyu Wang, Ryan P. Kelly, Adrianne L. Jenner, David J. Warne, Christopher Drovandi 1 School of Mathematical Sciences, Queensland University of Technology, Brisbane, QLD, Australia 2 Centre for Data Science, Queensland University of Technology, Brisbane, QLD, Australia. Computational models are invaluable in capturing the complexities of real-world biological processes. Yet, the selection of appropriate algorithms for inference tasks, especially when dealing with real-world observational data, remains a challenging and underexplored area.

arxiv-2502-16845.title: Uncovering simultaneous breakthroughs with a robust measure of disruptiveness
arxiv-2502-16845.creator: Munjung Kim, Sadamori Kojaku, Yong-Yeol Ahn
arxiv-2502-16845.description: Abstract Progress in science and technology is punctuated by disruptive innovation and breakthroughs. Researchers have characterized these disruptions to explore the factors that spark such innovations and to assess their long-term trends. However, although understanding disruptive breakthroughs and their drivers hinges upon accurately quantifying disruptiveness, the core metric used in previous studies—the disruption index—remains insufficiently understood and tested.

arxiv-2502-19721.title: Unsupervised Concept Vector Extraction for Bias Control in LLMs
arxiv-2502-19721.creator: Hannah Cyberey, Yangfeng Ji, David Evans
arxiv-2502-19721.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are known to perpetuate stereotypes and exhibit biases. Various strategies have been proposed to mitigate these biases, but most work studies biases as a black-box problem without considering how concepts are represented within the model. We adapt techniques from representation engineering to study how the concept of “gender” is represented within LLMs.

arxiv-2507-13443.title: easyspec : An open-source Python package for long-slit spectroscopy Facilities: TNG(DOLORES), SOAR(Goodman)
arxiv-2507-13443.creator: Raniere de Menezes, Francesco Massaro, Michela Negro, Claudia M. Raiteri, Harold Peña-Herazo, Jose A. Acosta-Pulido
arxiv-2507-13443.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Raniere de Menezes, Francesco Massaro, Michela Negro, Claudia M. Raiteri, Harold Peña-Herazo, Jose A. Acosta-Pulido. In modern-day astronomy, near-infrared, optical, and ultraviolet spectroscopy are indispensable for studying a wide range of phenomena, from measuring black hole masses to analyzing chemical abundances in stellar atmospheres. However, spectroscopic data reduction is often performed using instrument-specific pipelines or legacy software well-established and robust within the community that are often challenging to implement and script in modern astrophysical workflows.

arxiv-2510-09075.title: Experimental overview: quarkonia as probes for deconfinement
arxiv-2510-09075.creator: \firstname Michael \lastname Winn \fnsep
arxiv-2510-09075.description: Abstract The current status of the experimental investigation of quarkonia in heavy-ion collisions as probes for deconfinement is reviewed. The emphasis is put on the qualitative understanding of charmonia ( c ​ c ¯ c\bar{c} bound states) and bottomonia ( b ​ b ¯ b\bar{b} ) based on the results in the past few years.

arxiv-2601-02952.title: The left-to-right minima basis of the group algebra of the symmetric group (updated version)
arxiv-2601-02952.creator: Darij Grinberg \addressmark 1, Ekaterina A. Vassilieva \addressmark 2
arxiv-2601-02952.description: Abstract We introduce a new basis of the group algebra of the symmetric group, built using the left-to-right minima sets of permutations. We show that on this basis, the descent algebra acts by triangular operators, thus making it an analogue of a cellular basis.

britannica-1911-quinones.title: Quinones (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-quinones.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-quinones.description: Article 'Quinones' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 22), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. This replacement may take place either in the ortho or para positions, giving rise to orthoquinones or to paraquinones; metaquinones do not appear to have been isolated. The para or true quinones are obtained by the oxidation of hydrocarbons with chromic acid or of various para di-derivatives of benzene with chromic acid mixture, such, for example, as para-aminophenol, para-phenylene diamine, para-aminoazobenzene, &c.

pmc-11337744.title: Independent risk factors of left ventricular hypertrophy in non-diabetic individuals in Sierra Leone - a cross-sectional study
pmc-11337744.creator: Yuanxin Xu, Yingxin Celia Jiang, Lihua Xu, Weiyu Zhou, Zhiying Zhang, Yanfei Qi, Hongyu Kuang, Shuang Yan
pmc-11337744.description: BackgroundLeft ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is a critical factor in heart failure and cardiovascular event-related mortality. While the prevalence of LVH in diabetic patients is well-documented, its occurrence and risk factors in non-diabetic populations remain largely unexplored. This study addresses this issue by investigating the independent risk factors of LVH in non-diabetic individuals.

pmc-11429399.title: Effect of a smartphone-based physical intervention on depression, fitness factors and movement characteristics in adults
pmc-11429399.creator: Hyungsook Kim, David Michael O’Sullivan
pmc-11429399.description: BackgroundPhysical activity has been shown to correlate with mental health and a reduction in symptoms of depression. However, the majority of research has focused only on the effects of either aerobic or nonaerobic exercise on depressive symptoms, while the use of novel technological innovations such as mobile phone-based activity programs and their effects on movement characteristics are underrepresented.

pmc-11585097.title: Impostor phenomenon and self- reported satisfaction among medical and surgical postgraduate trainees in Sri Lanka
pmc-11585097.creator: Manudi Vidanapathirana, Deshan Gomez, Inoshi Atukorala
pmc-11585097.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPsychological phenomena such as impostor phenomenon (IP) and low work-related satisfaction increase the risk of burnout among medical professionals. The prevalence of these contributory risk factors among South Asian medical professionals has not been examined thus far.

pmc-11684464.title: A Rare Case Report of Dengue Fever Presenting With Acute Leukoencephalopathy With Restricted Diffusion
pmc-11684464.creator: Soham N Naik
pmc-11684464.description: Acute leukoencephalopathy with restricted diffusion (ALERD) is an emerging clinico-radiological syndrome marked by sudden onset encephalopathy and characteristic restricted diffusion in the subcortical white matter on MRI. While typically linked to other viral etiologies, its association with dengue fever is not well known and is rarely documented in the literature.

pmc-11715775.title: Biomarker Evaluation in Young Onset Dementia from Diverse Populations
pmc-11715775.creator: Eden V Barragan, Hilary W Heuer, Rachel L Nosheny, Monica R Camacho, Krista Navarra, Paul S S Aisen, Annalise Rahman‐Filipiak, J Scott Roberts, Adeyinka Ajayi, Desiree Byrd, Monica Rivera Mindt, Gil D Rabinovici, Adam L Boxer
pmc-11715775.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEarly onset dementia (EOD) affects people at the peak of their personal and professional responsibilities and economic productivity. Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) are the most common EOD etiologies in Non‐Latinx White adults (NLW). Black and Latinx older adults bear a disproportionate burden of dementia compared to NLW, likely due to vulnerabilities that confer increased risk, such as cardiovascular factors, socioeconomic stressors, and structural racism.

pmc-12412673.title: “Deep Brain Stimulation of the Ventral Intermediate Nucleus of the Thalamus for Tremor in Polr3a-Related Tremor-ataxia Syndrome: A Two-case Report”
pmc-12412673.creator: Edgar Javier Sánchez-Román, Leonel Villa-Villegas, Roberto Leal-Ortega, Luz Gabriela Lira-Jaime, Francisco Rivas-Ruvalcaba, Karely Díaz-Ramírez, Carlos Eduardo Piña-Avilés, Rodrigo Mercado-Pimentel, Carlos Zúñiga-Ramírez
pmc-12412673.description: Clinical Vignette:RNA polymerase III subunit A (POLR3A) related disorders are a group of heterogeneous diseases with a recessive autosomic inheritance. These disorders manifest with distinct clinical features like ataxia, spasticity, hypodontia, hypogonadism, mental retardation and progressive motor decline.Clinical Dilemma:POLR3A gene mutation can manifest with parkinsonism, dystonia, ataxia and tremor. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) might be effective for motor symptoms.

pmc-12578919.title: Assessment of knowledge, attitudes and behaviors related to self-medication practices among the adult population during the COVID-19 pandemic in Italy
pmc-12578919.creator: Concetta Paola Pelullo, Chiara Lombardi, Giorgia Della Polla, Francesco Napolitano, Gabriella Di Giuseppe
pmc-12578919.description: This study evaluated the knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors about self-medication practices during the COVID-19 pandemic and any changes from the period before the current health emergency. A cross-sectional study was conducted from June to December 2021 in the Campania region, Southern of Italy. Of the 590 questionnaires distributed, 525 returned for an overall response rate of 89%. Overall, 66.

pmc-12785355.title: Real-World Utility of GWAS-Based Diabetes Mellitus Panel Testing
pmc-12785355.creator: In Hwa Jeong, Kyung-Won Hong, Ja-Eun Choi, Bo-Kyung Shine
pmc-12785355.description: This study evaluated the clinical utility of a polygenic risk score (PRS)-based multigene panel test for predicting diabetes mellitus (DM) in a healthy population. A total of 302 individuals underwent genetic testing using the HelloGene™ DM panel, which includes four DM-related single nucleotide polymorphisms (CDKAL1, HHEX, KCNQ1, and TCF7L2).
